A computer is a system of connected parts, power, firmware, storage, memory, and software. Follow the path below while you work on a real classroom computer. The topic comes first; the CS code is only a short label for the activity package.

## Learning path

::: {.ter-path-grid}
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 1. Know the parts

Identify the motherboard, processor, memory, storage, cooling, power supply, ports, and expansion connections.

[CS02: Parts and baseline inspection](cs02-parts-baseline-esd.qmd)
:::

::: {.ter-path-card}
### 2. Understand computer power

Connect voltage, current, resistance, and power to the parts inside a computer.

[CS01: Electricity bridge](cs01-electricity-bridge.qmd)
:::

::: {.ter-path-card}
### 3. Open and inspect

Power down, unplug, open the case, check the condition, and record what is installed.

[CS02: Parts and baseline inspection](cs02-parts-baseline-esd.qmd)
:::

::: {.ter-path-card}
### 4. Check the power connections

Trace the main power paths and check that each connector is seated in the correct place.

[CS03: Power and connections](cs03-power-connections.qmd)
:::

::: {.ter-path-card}
### 5. Start the computer

Use a ready-to-power check, observe the first boot, and separate a power fault from a startup fault.

[CS04: First boot](cs04-ready-to-power.qmd)
:::

::: {.ter-path-card}
### 6. Understand POST and BIOS/UEFI

Read startup evidence and use firmware settings to identify hardware, boot order, and common problems.

[CS05: POST and BIOS/UEFI](cs05-post-firmware.qmd)
:::

::: {.ter-path-card}
### 7. Install an operating system

Choose the correct target drive, install Linux Mint, create accounts, update the system, and verify the hardware.

[Open the canonical Linux Mint guide](../linux-operating-systems/install-linux-mint.qmd)
:::

::: {.ter-path-card}
### 8. Upgrade RAM or storage

Check compatibility, install the part, and prove that the computer recognizes it.

[CS07: RAM upgrade](cs07-ram-upgrade.qmd) · [Storage extension](sq03-storage-expansion.qmd)
:::

::: {.ter-path-card}
### 9. Benchmark and compare

Run the same test before and after a change, keep the raw evidence, and explain the result.

[CS08: Benchmark challenge](cs08-benchmark-challenge.qmd) · [Performance notes](../linux-operating-systems/performance-benchmarking.qmd)
:::

::: {.ter-path-card}
### 10. Troubleshoot, repair, and reuse

Use symptoms, tests, evidence, and one change at a time to recover useful hardware.

[Fault stations](sq02-fault-stations.qmd) · [Repair and reuse](sq06-repair-reuse.qmd)
:::
:::
